details: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has downgraded its global growth forecast to 3.1%, warning that the world economy could face a recession if the ongoing US-Iran conflict intensifies and oil prices remain elevated through 2027. This fragile macroeconomic outlook has weighed on digital assets, with Bitcoin recently trading around $74,000, significantly down from its $126,000 peak. However, some analysts suggest that rising global public debt, projected to approach 100% of global GDP by 2029 by the IMF, could make Bitcoin a long-term bullish indicator as investors seek alternatives outside traditional finance. The tightening liquidity due to high interest rates also contributes to the current struggle in crypto prices.
title: Global Recession Warning from IMF Sparks Crypto Volatility

details: Markets have seen a rally in risk assets, including Bitcoin, driven by optimism over potential peace talks between the US and Iran. President Donald Trump's signals of potential negotiations have fueled this "risk-on" sentiment. Bitcoin recently reached a four-week high, climbing as much as 4% to $76,094 before paring gains to trade around $74,000. Smaller tokens like Ethereum also advanced, reaching over $2,400. This positive sentiment is helping to offset fears of an energy shock sparking global inflationary pressures.
title: Optimism for US-Iran Peace Talks Boosts Risk Assets and Bitcoin

details: The European Central Bank (ECB) is closely watching the economic impact of the Middle East conflict, which has led to increased volatility in equity and bond markets and a surge in energy prices. While an upcoming ECB meeting is widely expected to result in a 25-basis point interest rate cut, marking a potential divergence from the Federal Reserve, some policymakers have hinted that a rate hike cannot be entirely ruled out if inflation expectations worsen. Financial markets currently expect at least two rate adjustments this year. The euro has depreciated against the US dollar due to the energy shock.
title: ECB Considers Rate Adjustments Amid Middle East Conflict

details: Goldman Sachs has filed for its first crypto-related exchange-traded fund (ETF), proposing a yield-focused, options-overlaid vehicle designed to hold spot Bitcoin ETFs from other issuers. This move aims to generate Bitcoin income while managing price volatility. Separately, crypto exchange Kraken is proceeding with its confidential initial public offering (IPO) filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission, despite a recent slide in its corporate valuation. Deutsche Börse Group has backed Kraken with a $200 million investment, securing a 1.5% stake.
title: Goldman Sachs Eyes Bitcoin ETF, Kraken Plans IPO
